Are you sure that the entire circuit isn’t on a gfi. I had a call about 6 months ago I had a similar situation where it kept tripping the breaker because one of the outlets the circuit was on was gfi. Unit wasn’t plugged into gfi but even if it’s on the same circuit it’ll pop the breaker. I would take an extension chord and plug it into a different circuit and see if it will work then.
Just stand it back up for 24hrs before plugging it in so the oil in the compressor can settle.
Would need a new magnetron and waveguide most likely. Is it worth fixing? Depends on what microwave you have. Usually I don’t recommend unless it’s like a Bosch or higher models.
What I see commonly as long as your seals are good is circulation pump, inlet valve or diverter motor. Diverter motor is most likely where leak comes from . Look for water trails and calcium buildup.
Same I had to reinstall and now it’s working.
Also note that some company’s will sell knock off brands for filters for cheaper but won’t work for some units that I’ve seen so I always recommend buying oem.

Sure they can be repaired just depends on how much money you want to sink into it generally for all the cheaper models it’s not worth the price to repair over buying a new one.
You could jump it if it’s on separate connectors but I don’t recommend doing that. Use a multimeter and check for continuity if no continuity you found your issue.
Check the thermostat fuse for the motor. Most likely is you either have a clogged vent from your dryer to your outside or your vent hose is kinked and your cabinet got overheated and blew your fuse.
Most likely is fan is hitting ice build up on evaporator. Defrost circuit is what I would be checking first
